summary: Mostly no. On BTC, ETH and SOL, closes below a lower 2σ band and shorts above an upper 2σ band did the same as random entries on 1h and 4h, and every long result above the weekly or monthly VWAP rests on one rally. The result that holds up is narrow: on SOL 1h, closes above the weekly VWAP beat random by 0.19%, without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h and 4h with the daily or the weekly anchor, in uptrends and in downtrends. On daily candles the weekly band was also same as random, and the daily band had too few separate moves to judge.

verdicts.use: Shorting the stretch (above the upper 2σ band)
verdicts.text: Same as random pooled on 1h and 4h. In downtrends on 1h the short beat random by 0.10%, at 10 and 20 candles only.

verdicts.use: Riding the trend (above the weekly VWAP)
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h and 4h, but each result rests on one rally. Only SOL on 1h held without its strongest stretch.

verdicts.use: Riding the trend (above the monthly VWAP)
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h, 4h and daily, but each gap comes from a single rally. Without it, price moved as it did after random candles.

notes: Closes below the daily VWAP's lower 2σ band on 1h gave 12,898 entries in 3,273 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.07% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band, and the same held in uptrends and in downtrends. The weekly lower band fires about half as often and was 0.09% behind random, also same as random. On BTC it looked worse than random on 1h and 4h, but only because of signals on Jun 10–14, 2022, during the Celsius withdrawal freeze.

Shorting closes above the daily VWAP's upper 2σ band was same as random pooled on 1h, at 0.05%. Split by trend, the result changes. In downtrends the short beat random by 0.10%, held without its strongest stretch, the Terra collapse on May 10–11, 2022, and showed at 10 candles but not at 50 or 100; in uptrends it showed nothing. On 4h the same short looked better than random in uptrends only because of the stretch between Nov 15, 2021 and Jan 18, 2022.

Closes above the weekly VWAP on 1h beat random by 0.08% pooled, but the gap rests on SOL's run between Oct 13, 2023 and Nov 13, 2023 and is same as random without it. Split by trend, it showed only in downtrends, and was fragile there as well. SOL alone held up: 0.19% ahead of random on 1h, without that stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, while BTC and ETH were same as random. On 4h the result, 0.22%, rests on the stretch between Jul 21, 2021 and Nov 15, 2021, and neither trend beat random.

Above the monthly VWAP the gap grows with the timeframe: 0.14% on 1h, 0.35% on 4h and 2.25% after 20 days on daily. Each rests on one rally, between Jan 1, 2021 and Mar 3, 2021 on 1h and between Dec 29, 2020 and Mar 3, 2021 on 4h, and is same as random without it. On 1h it showed in uptrends, fragile there too, and not in downtrends. On 4h it showed in neither trend, and on daily it showed nothing in downtrends.

Closes above the daily VWAP on 1h enter about six and a half times as often as the lower 2σ band and were same as random, at -0.02%, on every pair and in both trends. On 4h and daily candles the daily anchor gives only 3 separate moves pooled, under the 30 the test needs, so those cells are not judged.

For a long DCA bot, a close below the lower 2σ band timed entries no better than a random candle on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit carry the result. Above the weekly or monthly VWAP works at most as a trend filter beside other conditions, and the gains it shows come from single rallies. The cells worth testing on your own pair are the 1h short above the daily upper 2σ band while the pair is below its 200-day SMA, with the bot's take profit set inside 20 candles, and the weekly VWAP filter on SOL 1h.
